title: Polymeric anti-platelet carriers for the precision-targeting of age-related cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases

sections.abstract:
The global aging population has increased the burden of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, which remain leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. In their pathogenesis, platelets not only promote thrombus formation but also exert proinflammatory effects that cause extensive inflammatory responses, accelerating atherosclerosis and endothelial dysfunction. Traditional systemic anti-platelet agents face considerable challenges in elderly patients due to the delicate balance between antithrombotic efficacy and bleeding risk. Polymeric anti-platelet carriers alter the risk-benefit balance between antithrombotic efficacy and bleeding complications through local, biomarker-guided drug delivery. This review systematically summarizes platelet dysfunction in age-related cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases and corresponding strategies for constructing precision-targeted polymeric carriers. We first summarize major platelet-related biomarkers that have emerged as actionable targets, including glycoprotein VI (GPVI), platelet-derived growth factor-B (PDGF-B) and its receptor PDGFR-β, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and disease-associated shear stress. We then review recent advances in surface engineering approaches for targeted delivery, with emphasis on ligand-guided targeting, biomimetic cloaking, and multivalent binding designs. Next, we discuss carrier architectures tailored to improve drug loading and enable controlled release, highlighting stimuli-responsive platforms that exploit thrombotic microenvironmental signals, such as acidic pH, enzyme enrichment, oxidative stress, and shear forces, to trigger site-specific drug liberation. We also outline synergistic strategies that integrate anti-inflammatory and thrombolytic actions with biomimetic features to more effectively manage cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders. Finally, we consider future opportunities for polymeric anti-platelet delivery systems, focusing on materials innovation, patient stratification and personalization, and translational considerations that will shape long-term clinical utility. Overall, this review underscores the promise of polymer-based anti-platelet carriers for the prevention and treatment of age-related cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases.

Keywords: Platelet-associated biomarkers, Polymeric carriers, Anti-Platelet carriers, Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases
sections.introduction:
The continued acceleration of global population aging has significantly increased the burden of age-related diseases, with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases now ranking among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide [ 1 , 2 ]. Thrombosis, the formation of pathological thrombi within blood vessels, is a core component of acute events such as myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke. Notably, vascular aging is closely associated with increased susceptibility to thrombosis, a link largely stemming from the characteristic shift in platelet phenotype towards a hyperreactive state [ 3 ]. In the elderly, platelets often exhibit enhanced reactivity, stronger aggregation capacity, and a more pronounced pro-inflammatory phenotype, changes that can accelerate the progression of atherosclerosis and increase the risk of catastrophic events [ 4 ]. Coupled with chronic low-grade inflammation [ 5 ] and age-related endothelial dysfunction, these platelet abnormalities present particularly complex clinical challenges for the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases in the elderly.

Traditional anti-platelet therapy still primarily relies on systemic drugs, most commonly aspirin and P2Y12 receptor inhibitors, but this strategy is often significantly limited in elderly patients. A trade-off often needs to be struck between achieving antithrombotic protection and avoiding serious bleeding, especially in frail elderly populations [ 6 ]. This contradiction intensifies with age. Multiple meta-analyses and clinical guidelines consistently emphasize that advanced age, particularly ≥75 years, is a significant predictor of major bleeding during anti-platelet therapy, with gastrointestinal bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage accounting for a particularly high proportion of adverse outcomes in high-risk populations [ 7 , 8 ]. For example, a meta-analysis of 8 studies involving 29,217 elderly patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) showed that dual anti-platelet therapy (DAPT) with prasugrel or ticagrelor significantly increased the risk of bleeding compared to clopidogrel (RR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.08-1.27) [ 8 ]. This susceptibility is further compounded by coexisting diseases, polypharmacy, frailty, and age-related pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic alterations, all of which contribute to increased inter-individual variability in drug response and undermine the effectiveness of standardized dosing regimens in elderly patients receiving antithrombotic therapy [ 6 ]. Meanwhile, increasing evidence suggests that dysregulation of molecular and biophysical signals in the diseased vascular microenvironment can promote excessive platelet activation, providing clear targets for precise intervention. These pathological clues include receptor upregulation or remodeling (e.g., glycoprotein VI, GPVI), disruption of the platelet-derived growth factor B (PDGF-B) and its receptor (PDGFR-β) signaling axis, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated with oxidative stress, and adverse biomechanical conditions including increased local shear stress [ 9 , 10 ]. Utilizing these biomarkers and microenvironmental triggering signals holds promise for decoupling antithrombotic efficacy from systemic bleeding risk to some extent.

Polymeric drug delivery systems are increasingly viewed as adaptable solutions to this unmet need [ 11 ]. Built from biodegradable and biocompatible materials, platforms such as nanoparticles, micelles, and microgels can be engineered with controllable size, surface properties, and drug-loading capacity. Crucially, these systems support advanced surface functionalization and the integration of stimuli-responsive modules, allowing carriers to remain relatively inert during circulation and to activate only upon encountering disease-defining signatures, such as reduced pH, elevated ROS, or specific enzymatic activity, or target structures including activated platelets and exposed collagen typical of an active thrombus or atherosclerotic plaque [ 12 ]. By harnessing such localized signals, polymeric carriers can enable on-demand release and higher drug concentrations at the lesion site while reducing off-target distribution and systemic exposure.

This review summarizes recent breakthroughs in the design and application of polymeric carriers for biomarker-guided anti-platelet therapies. First, the platelet-associated biomarkers in age-related cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases and advancements in surface engineering to enhance their targeting specificity are discussed. Subsequently, the development of stimuli-responsive drug delivery systems that utilize pathological microenvironmental changes for precise drug release are described. Synergistic anti-platelet strategies that integrate anti-inflammatory, thrombolytic, or biomimetic mechanisms for excellent therapeutic outcomes are then discussed. Finally, major translational hurdles concerning safety, scale-up, and patient-specific optimization are discussed to provide a future perspective on avenues through which innovations in material science and personalized medicine will pave the way for the clinical implementation of polymeric anti-platelet systems in the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases [ 13 , 14 ].
